summary: Program layout for team review, November 2026.

LT1.theme: Safety, equipment and tools; lighting basics (incandescent, fluorescent); project and retrofit work

LT2.theme: Circuits and measurement; HID and LED systems; troubleshooting; prints and emergency lighting; service work; track and low-voltage

LT3.theme: Exterior and pole work; controls; refrigerated case, neon, signage and data cabling

LT4.theme: Senior: networked controls, codes, photometry, power quality, advanced troubleshooting, qualified-worker safety

LT5.theme: Master: audits and estimating, commissioning, leadership, emerging technology, maintenance planning, capstone

owner_changes_internal: Nov 11: fluorescent split to LT1 #11; HID LT2; Project Readiness to be reframed (projects first, then service calls); Print Reading LT2 #6; Emergency & Egress LT3->LT2 #7.

additions.title: Stop Work, Regroup and Call Your Supervisor
additions.covers: Full authority to stop a job for a safety concern or when it can't be done to our quality expectations; how to make the area safe, call the supervisor, regroup and get approval to restart.

additions.title: First Aid, CPR/AED and Emergency Response
additions.covers: Recognizing emergencies, calling 911, bleeding control, burns, electrical shock first response, falls, heat and cold illness, eye injuries; where the first-aid kit, AED and fire extinguisher are and how to use them; our incident reporting. Recommend pairing with a certified first aid/CPR/AED class.

additions.title: Multi-Position (Articulating) Ladder Setup
additions.covers: Each mode (A-frame, extension, stairway, scaffold), locking hinges and confirming they are locked, carrying and setup as two-person work, with a hands-on sign-off.

additions.title: Lamp Recycling, Universal Waste and PCB Ballasts
additions.covers: Which lamps contain mercury and why all lamps are recycled; packing, labeling, storing and logging lamps, batteries and ballasts; identifying PCB ballasts (no 'No PCBs' label, pre-1979, date codes), handling leaking ballasts, separate packaging and special disposal paperwork; lithium battery handling.

additions.title: Biological and Public-Site Hazards
additions.covers: Needles and sharps in public areas and fixtures, bird and rodent droppings (histoplasmosis), wasps and insects in fixtures and poles, cleanup PPE and when to stop and report.

additions.title: Tool Fundamentals (test-out available)
additions.covers: Built for someone who has never used tools: tool identification, drills and impact drivers (batteries, clutch, bits), hand tools, measuring (imperial and metric), ratchet straps, cords and chargers; what a concrete saw, pipe bender and rotary hammer are for (awareness only). The LT1 personal tool list. Techs who pass a hands-on test-out can skip it.

additions.title: Wire Strippers and Cutters: Keep Your Body Off Grounded Metal
additions.covers: Added to the existing hand-tools lesson: no part of your hand or arm touching metal (T-bar, fixture housing) while stripping or cutting, using a real 277 V shock as the example.

additions.title: Vehicles, Trailers and Load Securement
additions.covers: Daily vehicle and trailer inspection; hooking up, inspecting and backing a trailer, with a backing test and supervisor sign-off; choosing and using the right ratchet straps; minor vehicle maintenance (headlight and turn-signal bulbs, battery replacement); cleaning out the vehicle at the end of each day and after each project.

additions.title: Customer Site Rules: Badging, Escorts, Security and Photos
additions.covers: Checking in and out, badges and escorts, restricted areas, alarm and door security, confidentiality, and when photos are and are not allowed.

additions.title: Truck Stock, Parts ID and Defective Equipment
additions.covers: Identifying common parts on the truck; minimum stock levels; recording what was used each day on the truck stock sheet so it can be replenished; inspecting, red-tagging and reporting defective tools, ladders and equipment.

additions.title: Electrical Safety and Arc-Flash Protection, Part 1: Awareness (draft module)
additions.covers: See the Electrical Safety Module tab. Boundaries, arc-flash labels and PPE categories, when work must be de-energized, test before touch, first response to a shock or arc flash.

additions.title: Repair or Replace: Our Decision Guide
additions.covers: What our company does in common situations: failed LED driver, MH400 ballast (corn-cob lamp vs ballast and lamp vs new fixture), aging fluorescent, discontinued parts, standard fixtures on the truck. Built on the mA and voltage basics; licensees can adapt it.

additions.title: Installation Tools
additions.covers: Tools for installing fixtures: step bits, hole saws, knockout punches, fish tape and rods, anchors and toggles, stud and joist finders, cutting ceiling tile and drywall cleanly. The LT2 personal tool list.

additions.title: Attics, Crawl Spaces and Tight Spaces
additions.covers: Recognizing permit-required confined spaces (stop and call), heat, insulation and dust, footing on joists, lighting and communication, getting out quickly.

additions.title: Traffic, Public Areas and Night Work
additions.covers: Cones and barricades, working in parking lots and drive lanes, spotters and flaggers, high-visibility gear, lighting your work area at night, and keeping the public out from under the work.

additions.title: Pole Installation Rigging: Slings, Shackles (Clevis) and Ratchet Straps
additions.covers: Selecting sling type and size, shackles and ratchet straps for setting a pole, working load limits, tag lines and signals for installs (not only removals).

additions.title: Large Tools: Rotary Hammer, Wire Tugger and Basic MIG Welding
additions.covers: Large-hole rotary hammer drilling in concrete (silica dust control), wire tugger setup and pulling, minor MIG welding for brackets and bases; hot-work permits, fire watch and PPE. The LT5 personal tool list.

LT4-C07: Electrical Safety and Arc-Flash Protection, Part 2: Qualified Worker (draft module)

names: Shock and Arc-Flash Safety for Lighting Technicians
part2: Shock and arc-flash boundaries: what they mean for you
Limited, restricted and arc-flash boundaries in plain language; who may cross each one; why an LT1 or LT2 stays outside.
Reading arc-flash labels and choosing PPE
What a label tells you, PPE categories, arc-rated clothing, face and hand protection, and what to do when there is no label.
De-energize first; the narrow reasons energized work is allowed; energized work permits; our company stance on lighting during business hours.
Live-dead-live under real conditions, meter and lead checks, CAT ratings, and the mistakes that hurt people.
First response to a shock or arc flash
Making the scene safe, never touching someone still in contact, calling 911, burns and cardiac risk, and reporting.
